> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23365eaedf5bd07795b3c3a47ff6f113469e5432` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `13f8e49843428b24665e3154a48324e0222b0dd6` — the merge of head `f6a9373da41384d11a45a095372965154643cce8` into base `23365eaedf5bd07795b3c3a47ff6f113469e5432`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 13f8e49843428b24665e3154a48324e0222b0dd6 && git checkout 13f8e49843428b24665e3154a48324e0222b0dd6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 23365eaedf5bd07795b3c3a47ff6f113469e5432 f6a9373da41384d11a45a095372965154643cce8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 23365eaedf5bd07795b3c3a47ff6f113469e5432 && git merge --no-ff f6a9373da41384d11a45a095372965154643cce8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23365eaedf5bd07795b3c3a47ff6f113469e5432
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 23365eaedf5bd07795b3c3a47ff6f113469e5432` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `be721ef6fbed24fca447774a5e13e1ae95eb7cf6`
Local-runs: none

Read-only and adversarial, on PR #21336 at the head above; merge base `5f7d84769a`, two commits (`e4d85c50b0`, `be721ef6fb`); the API diff and `git diff 5f7d8476..be721ef6` agree hunk for hunk (11 files, +737 / −96). Inputs: card #21242 (body and all ten comments), ruling 5933322270 on #21109 (letter A), the services declaration 5945507305 on #21118, the #21299 pointer 5944816815, the PR body, file list and diff, and the head's check-runs, read last. One caution for the seat: the shared checkout's `FETCH_HEAD` was moved by another fetch between my fetch and my first grep, so every reading below was re-taken against the literal sha.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The deletion — right.** At the head `packages/formula/src/matches-filter.ts` has no `lteBound`: the function, its docblock, the `addWholeDays` bullet naming it, and the `nextUtcCalendarDay` / `isUnboundedAbove` imports are gone; `$lte` and the `$between` maximum use the same `order()` the other ordering arms use, with an inclusive at-most test; the `9999-12-31` no-bound special case went with it and now lives only in `lowerFilterCondition` (a lone `$lte` on that day lowers to `{ $null: false }`, pinned). No replacement copy: repo-wide `lteBound` hits at the head are the F11 preview copy in `service-analytics/src/preview-evaluator.ts` (another face, ADR-0053 D-D1 item 9, its own deletion card, untouched), two rows of `docs/design/predicate-compilation-convergence.md`, the stale `driver-sql` conformance note and one `service-analytics` test docblock — all pre-existing. This is the ruling's "deleted mechanically".

2. **The caller table — right, re-derived.** `git grep matchesFilterCondition` at the head, tests, dist and prose excluded: 4 production call sites in 2 packages — `objectql/src/having-filter.ts:1657`, `plugin-security/src/rls-check-stored-form.ts:316`, `plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts:972`, `plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:3622`; `formula/src/index.ts:118` is the re-export and `matches-filter.ts:331` the definer, which is what the first count's "3 packages" counted. Tenant wall: `tenantLayer0FilterOf` (`tenant-layer.ts:170-180`) emits only `organization_id` equality, `$in` or the deny filter, so no bound reaches it — unchanged by construction. Explain: `explain-engine.ts` compiles nothing itself (it imports `RLS_DENY_FILTER` and `compiledPolicyNameOf` only); it judges the `using` filter the plugin compiled at the guard site, so its row verdict moves with the read. A non-storage bound still reaches three callers (a per-row `{ $field }` referent at `having-filter`; non-`datetime` columns at the write check and at explain); each changed answer is recorded in the PR body and the changesets and pinned at the evaluator (`formula`) and at `engine.aggregate` (`objectql`). The write-check cells on `text` columns (R1–R3) and explain's verdicts are recorded, not pinned end to end in `plugin-security` — see ③.

3. **The `objectql` pins — right.** H2 falsified as stated: no ORDERS row and no DT_ROWS group closes on its due day, so both registry-less pins keep `picked: 3` and `['c1']`; each is kept and extended with one boundary row (`o7` / `c4`, closed at 15:00 on the due day) whose answer records the move (4 of 7 becomes 3 of 7; `['c1', 'c4']` becomes `['c1']`). The residual rows of #21299 are pinned: audit-opt-out `created_at` / `updated_at` against `due_on` at the per-aggregation filter (3 of 4 becomes 1 of 4, both drivers, the audit-on object refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 as the control) and direct `applyInMemoryAggregation` (3 of 4 becomes 1 of 4, with and without a field map). The unanticipated mainline row — two declared `text` columns of one class, `code $lte { $field: 'label' }` with `'2026-01-05 noon'` against `'2026-01-05'` — is a correct change at a public door: one class, so the #21255 rule does not refuse it; a per-row referent, so no seam lowers it; the old count read a text label as a calendar day, and the new one is the `where` twin's (`driver-sql` keeps `b2` only). It is pinned at the per-aggregation filter (2 of 4) and at `having` over two groupBy columns (`['2026-01-04']`), and it is named in the `formula` changeset's `engine.aggregate` list. No `objectql` changeset is owed: `objectql` source is untouched.

4. **The `formula` test moves — right; nothing deleted or weakened.** The 8 assertions whose answer changed (the three instants under `$lte '2026-07-28'`, the `$between` at 21:40, `9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z`, the `Date` at 10:00 on that day, the same-day `$between` on `9999-12-31`, and `9999-12-30T10:00Z`) each keep a whole-day leg through `lowerFilterCondition(…, { isDatetimeColumn })` and gain an as-written leg; the lowered shapes are pinned (`$lt` the next day, `{ $null: false }`, the split `$between`). Every unchanged assertion is kept (the next-day stop, the plain calendar day, the full-ISO bound, `$gte` / `$gt` / `$lt`, the impossible day, the null bound, the no-instant text value), and one case is new (a number against a day string is false). `matches-filter-field-reference-offset.test.ts`: the calendar-day case moves to a stored `date` input with both assertions intact; the old instant-against-day input is re-pinned as written (false at `addDays: 1`, true at `2`) and refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 once the columns are declared (`MatchesFilterOptions.fields` is the right shape). `matches-filter-temporal-conformance.test.ts`: every `TEMPORAL_CASES` filter runs through the lowering with `{ at: datetime, on: date }`, expected rows unchanged. One leg (the `9999-12-30` control's negative) now runs through the seam only; as written it is false too, so nothing is weakened.

5. **The RLS compile seam — right, and one rule.** Guard: `RlsFieldGuard.number`, filled by `noteNumberMeta` in `loadObjectFieldNames` on both `fields` shapes, set beside `datetimeFieldNamesCache` (`security-plugin.ts:9315-9316`) and cleared beside it in the metadata watch (`:1433`); `fieldNamesCache` has one setter (`:9227`) in the same pass, so `declared` and `number` cannot diverge, and both guard sites (`:7463`, `:7735`) pass it. Verdict imported, not copied: `numberComparandFieldVerdict`, `numberComparandDoorVerdict`, `numberComparandRefusalMessage`, `NUMBER_COMPARAND_DOOR_SCALAR_OPERATORS` and `NUMBER_COMPARAND_DOOR_LIST_OPERATORS` from `@objectstack/spec/data` — the same five names `objectql/src/number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts` imports; no grammar is restated. Order: `assertListComparandShapes`, then `narrowPolicyNumberComparands`, then `normalizeFilterComparandTypes`, then `lowerFilterCondition` — the engine's relative order (`engine.ts:1027`, `:1075`, `:1085`, `:1251`). Refusal: the thrown `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 is caught by the existing `catch` and returned as `refused-comparand`, so the policy is dropped for the clause being compiled; the new pin file records `check:refused-comparand` and `using:refused-comparand` on each of three predicates, 403 on the write and the deny sentinel on the read. Numeric string: `narrows` replaces the comparand copy-on-write (`out ??= { ...spec }`), provenance carried by `withProvenanceOf`. Guard absent: nothing judged, the shape `datetime` already takes. The walk itself is the seam's own: `objectql`'s `narrowNumberComparands` is not a package export and `objectql` is a devDependency of `plugin-security`, so a shared walker cannot be imported; the positions walked are the spec's operator lists, and `$field` references and dotted keys are skipped as the engine skips them. PR #21235's pins: `rls-check-stored-form.ts` and its test are byte-identical between base and head; their verdict is the `Test Core` rollup (③).

6. **The four RLS cells — right.** R1 (`text` under a bare-day `$lte`, written as an instant), R2 (`'2026-01-05 noon'`), R3 (`text` against a `text` referent holding a bare day): write admitted becomes 403, read hidden throughout, explain visible becomes hidden. R4 (`number` under `$lte '9999-12-31'`): the deletion alone opened write 403 / read shown; with the seam, write 403 / read hidden / explain hidden, `refused-comparand` on both clauses. Every cell now gives one answer on read and write. Pinned: R4 (three refusal predicates), the numeric-string cells (`'10'` under `$lte` and `==` at 5, 50, 10 and 11), the controls (a numeric literal; a `text` column compared as written). The declared-column controls (`date` / `datetime` on the boundary day, `datetime $lte '9999-12-31'`) are unchanged, as the stored-form check and the `datetime` lowering carry them.

### ② Semver level

- **Declared:** `@objectstack/formula` `minor` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` `minor`, each with a bang summary, a `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at line start, and one ADR-0087 marker reading `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why. `breakingDeclaration` reads all three signals plus the narrowing arm; `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:adr-0087-registration`) are green on the head. `minor` is the launch-window guard's level for a breaking narrowing (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`; #21255 and the engine door 4a1df19 use the same sentence). **Consistent.**
- **The `== '10'` cell.** Rule applied: the Clause-② value answers one question — 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 — and the arm records the breaking direction; `yes (narrowing)` is reserved for a diff that widens one surface and narrows another (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`). A numeric string naming its number is the declared contract since #20336 (`numberComparandDoorVerdict` answers `narrows`), and the read already showed the row, so the check admitting that write is the check pulled back to the declared contract, which the lane rules say does not touch Clause ② (`lanes/spec.md`: 收窄仍是契约面,不触条款②; `triage-duties.md`: 拉回已声明契约 ⇒ 代裁车道). Precedents: the engine door 4a1df19 (#20351) declared `no (narrowing)` while its `"12"` to `12` narrowing admitted rows on `InMemoryDriver` that matched nothing before — the same shape; d2bc644 (#21238) says in words that a write-check admission toward the read "is a security-floor behaviour change, not the declared widening" (its `yes (widening)` was earned by a new `core` export); and ruling 5933322270's execution parameter has a read/write-agreement move named in the changeset under the `no` value. **`no (narrowing)` is the right line**, and naming the admit in the changeset body is the precedent's form.
- **Prose, before / now / remedy:** accurate on every cell (they match the dev's table and the pins) and on the remedy (`lowerFilterCondition(filter, { isDatetimeColumn })`; compare a number with a number). One sentence is wrong in the `plugin-security` changeset: "No export or published type changes." `RLSCompiler` is a root export and `compileFilter(…, fieldGuard?: RlsFieldGuard)` is public, so `RlsFieldGuard` is reachable from the entry type graph and gains the optional `number` member — a published type change, additive and optional. It is not an accept-set widening (an absent guard judges nothing, exactly as `datetime` already works) and does not move the Clause-② value; the sentence should read "no export changes; the guard type `RLSCompiler.compileFilter` takes gains an optional `number` member". The same sentence in the `formula` changeset is true (`lteBound` was never exported). One more sentence is stated as fact without a live run: "PostgreSQL refuses to bind such text against a numeric column" — consistent with the spec door's own `boundByDriver` wording, and recorded by the dev as not measured on live PG. Changeset prose is the seat's sentence-by-sentence ACCEPT face, so both go to the seat as corrections owed before ACCEPT, not as grounds here.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **H1 (count falsified) — confirmed:** 4 sites in 2 packages; the definer is not a caller.
- **H2 (the pins do not move) — confirmed:** keeping both pins and adding one boundary row each is the right form; a rewritten pin would have lost the as-written reading.
- **H5 (refined) — right:** `formula`'s `package.json` depends on `@marcbachmann/cel-js` and `@objectstack/spec` only; ADR-0053 D-D1 item 4 names that edge as the reason the lowering lives in `@objectstack/spec/data`, item 5 is the "comparison it wrote" reading for a caller that passes no seam, and item 9 the interim copies. The citations in the code and the changesets hold. Item 10's open question (an in-repo caller carrying a bare-day bound a deleted copy would have widened) is answered for this face by the dev's producer count (examples: 0 `having`, 0 `$field`, 3 RLS predicates, all equality).
- **Out-of-scope notes, dispositions:**
  - `withoutWholeDayCopy` wrapper and header in `rls-check-stored-form.test.ts`: redundant at the head; the pins still assert equivalent semantics (`$lt`-or-`$eq` equals `$lte` as written). A cleanup rider for the services seat when it next touches the file; no card, and not this PR (a cross-lane file outside the declared surface).
  - `docs/design/predicate-compilation-convergence.md:361`, the F7 row: now false. A hand-written design doc with no gate; PD #10 puts it in the acceptance notes. A one-row correction may ride in this PR (it is the ruling's own investigation doc) or in the F11 deletion card, which edits the same table; not blocking.
  - `driver-sql/src/cross-field-conformance-cases.ts:145` ("memory `lteBound`"): stale before this PR; acceptance note, no card.
  - The RLS WARN wording: `numberComparandRefusalMessage` is called with `boundByDriver` defaulted (the `where` wording, naming PostgreSQL's server error) and a path rooted at `where`; true of `using`, not of `check`, WARN detail only. This one is the PR's own new sentence in its own declared file, and `compileFilter` knows the clause, so it owes a fix: in this PR (`boundByDriver` true for `using` only, the path rooted at the clause) or as a filed card — 承接者:无 is not a carrier for a sentence the seam itself prints. Not blocking: no author is shown it.
  - Residual rows to #21299: pinned here; the `text` / `text` row agrees with `where` and is not fail-open. Right; #21299's enumeration pin carries them.
- **Not pinned end to end:** R1–R3 and explain's verdicts are recorded in the PR body and the changesets and pinned at the evaluator, not at the `plugin-security` door. The card's bar ("same answer, or a recorded, storage-form-decided answer") is met; one `text`-column cell in `rls-number-comparand-door.test.ts` would close the gap cheaply. The seat's call.
- **#20822:** not closed by this PR (`Fixes #21242` only; `Part-of PR must not also close its card` green); the seat closes it at landing per 5941587176.
- **Governed surfaces:** none of the 11 paths is governed (`.changeset/`, `packages/formula`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security`); `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green.
- **Check-runs on the head, read last.** First reading 2026-10-02T05:40:10Z: 32 runs, 28 complete and green or skipped, four in progress (`Test Core (1/6)`, `(5/6)`, `(6/6)`, `Type Check · workspace`), so the required `Test Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` contexts were not yet verdicts then. Final reading 2026-10-02T05:45:30Z: 34 runs, every one complete, 31 `success` and 3 `skipped` by design (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), none red. The seven required contexts all conclude `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates` 05:38:23Z, `TypeScript Type Check` 05:41:09Z, `Test Core` 05:44:48Z, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 05:31:03Z, `Build Core` 05:28:21Z, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` 05:31:23Z, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` 05:23:26Z. `Test Core` green is the verdict on PR #21235's `rls-check-stored-form` pins and on the new `rls-number-comparand-door` pins. The PR is still a draft; readying, queueing and the #20822 close stay the seat's acts.
